newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei recovers to end up in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei recovers to end up in cautious trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures recovered to ended higher on Thursday despite renewed fears of an interest rate hike.
Dealers said the dollar's limited fall against the yen helped underpin the Nikkei.

The Nikkei 225 June contract hit a low of 17,960 after Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the International Finance Bureau, had voiced concerns over the yen's excessive decline against the greenback.
The June contract ended 20 points higher, at 18,075 on a turnover of 9,150 lots.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 347.2 against its previous close at 357.2. Turnover was at 1,620 lots.

According to Perry Gilbert, vice president of Refco Singapore Pte Ltd, the profit-taking on the Taiwan futures was triggered by nervousness over reports of a rescheduling of Taiwan government's cut in stock holdings in public companies.
